w: Anterior cord syndrome spares dorsal column function and gives bilateral motor and pain loss.
Posterior cord syndrome affects proprioception and vibration bilaterally.
p: Brown-Sequard: ipsilateral weakness and loss of proprioception, contralateral pain and temperature loss; cervical lesions add ipsilateral Horner syndrome.

w: Ectopic PTHrP from squamous tumors gives hypercalcemia without anemia and plasma cell disease.
Excess PTH from the parathyroids rarely causes this degree of hypercalcemia with renal failure and anemia.
p: Multiple myeloma causes CRAB features: hypercalcemia, renal failure, anemia and bone lesions.

w: Terbutaline is for uterine tachysystole, which has resolved with 3 contractions in 10 minutes.
Emergent cesarean is for persistent fetal compromise unresponsive to measures.
p: Variable decelerations from cord compression improve with repositioning and amnioinfusion, which cushions the cord.

w: Biopsy is reserved for atypical or uncertain presentations.
A Wood's lamp detects fluorescence of some fungal and bacterial infections.
p: Plaque psoriasis is a clinical diagnosis: well-demarcated erythematous plaques with silvery scale and the Auspitz sign.

bw: Thin upper lip, sunken nasal bridge, small jaw
w: Trisomy 21 gives upslanting palpebral fissures, flat facies and AV canal defects.
Fragile X causes a long face, macroorchidism and large ears, not this midface hypoplasia.
p: Fetal alcohol syndrome: growth restriction, microcephaly, smooth philtrum, thin upper lip, ADHD-like behavior and cardiac defects.

bw: No gain from exercise, aspirin and cilostazol
w: Amputation is for critical limb ischemia not amenable to revascularization.
Surgical decompression treats compartment syndrome.
p: Lifestyle-limiting claudication refractory to exercise and medical therapy is treated with endovascular or surgical revascularization.

w: Nasogastric lavage risks further perforation after caustic ingestion.
Steroids do not treat perforation and increase infection risk.
p: Esophageal perforation (Boerhaave or caustic injury) causes mediastinitis and needs prompt surgical repair, antibiotics and NPO status.

w: Hyperinsulinemia from obesity can accelerate puberty but does not itself prove a central GnRH response.
Cortisol overproduction (Cushing) delays puberty and causes growth failure.
p: Central precocious puberty: premature activation of the pulsatile GnRH generator; a leuprolide stimulation test shows a pubertal LH rise.

bw: Urge incontinence triggered by running water
w: Surgery is for stress incontinence or refractory cases.
Tibial nerve stimulation is a later option after behavioral and drug therapy.
p: Urge incontinence is managed first with bladder training and pelvic floor exercises, then antimuscarinics or beta-3 agonists.

bw: Contact lens wearer, painful red eye
w: Topical steroids worsen bacterial keratitis and are avoided before cultures.
Ganciclovir is for herpetic keratitis, which gives dendritic ulcers.
p: Contact lens bacterial keratitis (Pseudomonas) is an emergency treated with intensive topical fluoroquinolones.

w: Live attenuated influenza vaccine is contraindicated in pregnancy.
Varicella is a live vaccine and is contraindicated in pregnancy.
p: Give Tdap at 27-36 weeks of every pregnancy to transfer pertussis antibodies; inactivated influenza is recommended in season.

bw: Cyanotic infant, squats and sweats during feeds
w: Knee-chest position raises SVR, which reduces right-to-left shunting; it does not lower pulmonary resistance.
Venous return is not the mechanism and would increase right-sided flow across the shunt.
p: Tet spells are treated with knee-chest position, oxygen, morphine and phenylephrine, all aimed at raising SVR relative to PVR.

w: Osteotomy is for young patients with dysplasia or early disease.
Arthroscopic debridement has no benefit for advanced osteoarthritis.
p: Total joint replacement is indicated for end-stage osteoarthritis with refractory pain and functional limitation.

w: Octreotide is used for acute bleeding, not long-term prophylaxis.
TIPS is rescue therapy for failed endoscopic and medical management.
p: Secondary prophylaxis of variceal bleeding combines nonselective beta-blockers (propranolol, nadolol) with repeated endoscopic band ligation.

w: Tricuspid atresia causes cyanosis with no right ventricular inflow.
Tetralogy of Fallot is cyanotic with a boot-shaped heart and is not linked to WPW.
p: Ebstein anomaly (atrialized right ventricle) is associated with accessory pathways and Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome.

w: Abruptio placentae causes painful bleeding with uterine tenderness.
Uterine atony causes postpartum, not antepartum, hemorrhage.
p: Placenta previa: painless third-trimester bleeding with risk factors including prior cesarean; avoid digital exams and deliver by cesarean.
